newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus denies board discussed hold on status change.
newsitem.headline: Airbus denies board discussed hold on status change.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus denied on Monday a German newspaper report that its supervisory board recently decided to put on hold talks aimed at changing from a partnership to a limited liability company.
"Airbus denies that the issue of a suspension of talks on its status change was raised in any shape or form at a recent supervisory board," a spokesman for Airbus Industrie said.

Germany's Welt am Sonntag reported on Sunday that Airbus's supervisory board had decided at a May 27 meeting, in Toulouse, France, to freeze the strategic change in status that had been announced in January.
The Airbus spokesman said the board meeting took place in Paris on that date but gave no details of the discussions.
The newspaper, noting the meeting's results had not yet been made public, said talks had become bogged down over how to split up the mix of civil and military programmes.
An industry source said the four Airbus partners met informally before the supervisory board meeting but those talks were outside the formal board deliberations.
Airbus is a partnership between French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.

The partners signed a memorandum of understanding in January to undertake a valuation process to decide what assets would be pooled in the new Airbus company, which is needed to improve competitiveness and face up to the threat of a pending merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
But differences on the scope and timing ucturing have created tensions within the partnership, which is formed as a "groupement d'interet economique" (GIE) under French law.
